# MAXGEN — The Maxwell Genealogy Standard (v2.0) — full text of opengenealogyai.org



---
## MAXGEN

An open standard · public domain · current release v2.0
Genealogy data that is honest about what it doesn't know.
MAXGEN is a free, open data standard for family history. Every fact carries its source and a confidence score. Conflicting evidence is kept, not deleted. Anyone can use it, build on it, or extend it. No permission required.

ReadWhat the standard is and why it exists
ListenEight podcast episodes, one per schema
DownloadThe seven schema files, every version





## The problem it solves

Genealogy has never had more to work with. Close to two billion records are online, archives scan more every year, volunteers transcribe registers by the million, and DNA testing has added a whole new kind of evidence. The formats we exchange that work in were designed for a simpler time: one birth year, one birthplace, one set of parents, written down as settled fact. Real family history rarely arrives that clean. A census says 1843; a gravestone says 1844. A father could be one of three men with the same name.

MAXGEN writes the doubt down. It stores **what the document says** separately from **what we think it means**, keeps every claim with its source and a 0-to-1 confidence score, and never overwrites anything. Several possible parents can coexist until the evidence resolves them. Every uncertainty becomes a lead worth chasing instead of a dead end, and as each new source corroborates a name or a date you watch the confidence climb. People can read it, researchers can check it, and AI can work with it without inventing anything, because confidence is a machine's native language.

MAXGEN is built to sit alongside the archives, record sites, and communities researchers already rely on, not to replace them. It is a shared language they can all speak. Every ancestor. Every source. Every honest doubt.

## The seven schemas

A schema is a written rule-set that says exactly what fields a record has and what each one means, so that any program can read a record written by any other program. MAXGEN has seven, and each has its own page and its own podcast episode.



## Three promises

1. **Nothing is ever deleted.** A retracted claim gets a retraction note; it does not vanish. The audit trail is permanent.
2. **Living people are protected by the schema itself.** A record about a person who may be alive is locked private no matter what any application does.
3. **Old records stay readable forever.** Within a major version, fields are never renamed or removed. See the [versioning policy](/versions/).

## Who it is for

- **Developers** building genealogy tools or AI agents: seven JSON Schema files at stable addresses, a changelog, fixtures, and a [validator](/validator/) that runs in your browser.
- **Genealogists and archivists** deciding whether to trust it: the [plain-English guide](/standard/), the [FAQ](/faq/), and the [podcasts](/podcasts/).
- **Institutions** who need to know how it is governed before adopting it: the [governance page](/governance/) and the [licence](/license/).

MAXGEN is short for the Maxwell Genealogy Standard, named for its author, Garlon Maxwell. It is stewarded by OpenGenealogyAI and dedicated to the public domain (CC0).


---
## The Standard

The Maxwell Genealogy Standard · v2.0 · CC0
# The Standard

MAXGEN is a language for describing family-history evidence. It is not a product, not a database, and not a website. It is a set of seven schemas (written rule-sets for data records) that any program can read and write, so that research done in one place can be understood everywhere else. This page is the whole standard in plain English. The exact rules live in the [schema files](/schemas/).

## 1. What is MAXGEN?

MAXGEN is an open JSON standard for representing genealogical evidence and the people it describes in a way that is **honest about uncertainty**.

Some or most genealogy formats today can hold one answer per fact. When two records disagree about who someone's father was, one has to win and the other is set aside. MAXGEN takes a different approach: **every claim is an assertion** with a confidence score, a source, and a timestamp. Nothing is overwritten. Several possible parents can coexist. Conflicting birth years both survive. The uncertainty is the data.

Five ideas define it:

1. **Uncertainty is data.** Every claim carries a 0-to-1 confidence score (section 4) and dates are ranges, because a census age is a guess and "spring 1847" is not a day.
2. **Evidence and interpretation are kept apart.** MaxRecord holds what a document says, exactly as written. MaxPerson holds what we think it means. You can change your mind about a person without touching the document.
3. **Nothing is ever deleted.** A wrong merge is reversed, not erased. A disputed reading gets a `disputed_by` entry. Every change has a who, a when, and a why.
4. **Privacy is built into the schema.** A record about a person who may be alive is locked to the most restrictive licence, `tier2-private`, and public systems answer "not found". DNA records are always private and never hold raw genetic data.
5. **Extensions are the escape hatch.** Each schema is closed, so validation is exact, but every schema has an `extensions{}` object that accepts anything. You never need to fork.

> **The core principle:** an assertion with low confidence and a real source is worth more than a certain-looking answer with no source. MAXGEN never invents. When the document is unclear, the confidence score says so.

## 2. How MAXGEN differs from GEDCOM

GEDCOM is the 1984 file format that almost every genealogy program can import and export. It is one of the great successes of the field: forty years of trees have moved between programs because of it, and GEDCOM 7 continues to modernise it. MAXGEN is not a replacement for exchanging finished trees. It is a companion for exchanging the **evidence and reasoning** behind a tree, a job GEDCOM was never asked to do. The two are meant to work together.

| | GEDCOM | MAXGEN |
|---|---|---|
| Format | Custom plain text (`.ged`) | JSON, validated by JSON Schema |
| Relationships | One answer | Several candidates, each with a confidence score |
| Uncertainty | Not represented | The point of the design |
| Source for each fact | Optional | Required on every assertion |
| Dates | A single value | Ranges (`year_min` / `year_max`) |
| Conflicts | Resolved before saving | Preserved and flagged |
| Living people | No enforcement | Locked private by the schema |
| Transcription provenance | None | MaxRecognition, down to word-level confidence |
| Name variants across languages | None | MaxName |
| AI readiness | Predates it | Embedding text, structured evidence, anti-hallucination rules in MaxTask |
| Control | A steering committee | Public domain (CC0); anyone may use, fork, or extend |

MAXGEN event types map to GEDCOM tags (RESI, EMIG, IMMI, CENS, NATU, PROB, WILL, MILI) so conversion runs in both directions.

## 3. The seven schemas

A schema is a written rule-set that says exactly what fields a record has and what each one means. MAXGEN began with three record types and has grown to seven, each covering one layer of the research process. Each has [its own page](/schemas/) with fields, an example and a podcast episode.

| Schema | What one record is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **MaxRecord** | One source document exactly as found, uninterpreted | [MaxRecord](/schemas/maxrecord/) |
| **MaxPerson** | One probable person: a bundle of scored, sourced assertions | [MaxPerson](/schemas/maxperson/) |
| **MaxTask** | One unit of research work for a human or an AI, with proof required | [MaxTask](/schemas/maxtask/) |
| **MaxDNA** | DNA match evidence linked to a person, always private | [MaxDNA](/schemas/maxdna/) |
| **MaxSource** | One place where records live, with coverage and access details | [MaxSource](/schemas/maxsource/) |
| **MaxRecognition** | One transcription of one image: who read it and how sure they were | [MaxRecognition](/schemas/maxrecognition/) |
| **MaxName** | One name and every form it has taken, with sources | [MaxName](/schemas/maxname/) |

How they fit together:

```
  document image ──► MaxRecognition (who read it, how confident, word by word)
                            │
                            ▼
                       MaxRecord (the document, exactly as written)
                            │  cited by
                            ▼
   MaxName ◄──────────  MaxPerson  ◄────── MaxDNA (genetic evidence, always private)
 (is "Makeswell"      (a probable person:
  the same name?)      every claim scored)
                            │  spawns
                            ▼
                        MaxTask (work for a human or an AI, with proof required)
                            ▲
                            │  where to look next
                        MaxSource (a catalogue of where records live)
```

Each schema can be adopted on its own. An archive that only wants to publish transcriptions with provenance can use MaxRecognition alone.

## 4. The confidence score

Every assertion carries a `confidence` value from 0.0 to 1.0. The numbers are anchored, not decorative:

| Score | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0.90 to 1.00 | The field appears verbatim in the source with no ambiguity. |
| 0.70 to 0.89 | Minor spelling or transcription variation; well attested. |
| 0.50 to 0.69 | Inferred from context, not stated explicitly. |
| 0.30 to 0.49 | Ambiguous or damaged source. |
| 0.00 to 0.29 | Best guess only. Recorded so it is not lost, not so it is believed. |

Scores must be honest. A consistent 0.4 is more valuable than an inflated 0.9. A person's `composite_confidence` combines all assertions, weighted by source quality, using a noisy-OR rule: independent sources that agree raise confidence, but never to certainty, and two assertions that trace to the same document are not counted twice.

Why this matters for AI: models that read handwriting, match records and draft leads need an honest confidence on every claim, a source they can be checked against, and the losing candidates as well as the winner. In our own benchmarks, ordinary keyword search returned 0 to 5 percent of the right records for queries with a partial name and an approximate year; meaning-based search over embedded text is the baseline for this field. That is why every schema has an `embedding_text` field or equivalent, why every claim cites a `source_record_id`, and why MaxTask requires an AI to return the evidence it found rather than a summary of what it believes.

## 5. JSON examples

A MaxPerson is a set of assertion arrays. Every field that says something about the person is an array, never a single value:

```json
{
  "person_id": "b1000000-0006-4000-8000-000000000006",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "is_living": false,
  "composite_confidence": 0.95,
  "name_assertions": [
    { "name_as_written": "Mary Todd", "name_type": "birth", "confidence": 0.95,
      "source_record_id": "a1b2c3d4-0003-4000-8000-000000000003",
      "asserted_by": "extractor-agent-haiku-001", "asserted_at": "2026-05-01T14:00:00Z" },
    { "name_as_written": "Mary Lincoln", "name_type": "married", "confidence": 0.99,
      "source_record_id": "a1b2c3d4-0003-4000-8000-000000000003",
      "asserted_by": "extractor-agent-haiku-001", "asserted_at": "2026-05-01T14:00:00Z" }
  ],
  "birth_assertions": [
    { "year_min": 1818, "year_max": 1818, "month": 12, "day": 13, "place_as_written": "Lexington, Kentucky",
      "confidence": 0.98, "source_record_id": "a1b2c3d4-0003-4000-8000-000000000003",
      "asserted_by": "extractor-agent-haiku-001", "asserted_at": "2026-05-01T14:00:00Z" }
  ],
  "redistribution_license": "public-domain",
  "asserted_by": "extractor-agent-haiku-001",
  "asserted_at": "2026-05-01T14:00:00Z"
}
```

Every schema page carries a full, validated example: [MaxRecord](/schemas/maxrecord/), [MaxPerson](/schemas/maxperson/), [MaxTask](/schemas/maxtask/), [MaxSource](/schemas/maxsource/), [MaxRecognition](/schemas/maxrecognition/), [MaxName](/schemas/maxname/). Paste any record into the [validator](/validator/) to check it.

### 5b. Contributor attribution

Credit travels with the data, not in a site footer. A MaxRecord carries an `attribution{}` object naming the contributor (`contributor_name`, `contributor_url`, `contributor_role`) and the organisation the document came from (`source_organization`, `source_organization_url`). Every assertion in a MaxPerson names who made it (`asserted_by`) and when (`asserted_at`), and cites the record it came from, so a person's page can list every contributor whose work touched that person. A MaxRecognition names its transcriber, human or model, with credentials. Attribution is part of the record and stays with it wherever the record is copied.

## 6. File extensions

MAXGEN uses two file extensions so record types can be told apart at a glance:

- **`.maxgen`** for MaxPerson records: `william_whitfield_1842.maxgen`
- **`.mxrecord`** for MaxRecord source documents: `1880_census_ohio_p42.mxrecord`

Both are ordinary JSON files. MaxTask records live in a work queue and are not usually stored as standalone files. Any `.json` file that validates against a schema is also a valid MAXGEN record; the extensions are a convenience, not a requirement.

## 7. Versioning

All seven schemas share one version number and move together. Within a major version, fields are never renamed or removed; changes are additive only. A breaking change means a new major version, a new address space, a migration guide, and a 30-day public comment period. Records written to any version stay readable forever. The full policy, the stability promise, and every released version with permanent download links are on the [versions page](/versions/).

## 8. Why JSON?

- **Human-readable and machine-readable.** No proprietary parser required; you can open a record in a text editor.
- **Supported everywhere.** Every modern programming language reads and writes JSON natively.
- **Validated by JSON Schema 2020-12.** Structure is enforced at the moment a record is written, not discovered later.
- **Embeddable.** A MAXGEN record can be fed to an AI embedding model without conversion, which is what makes meaning-based search possible.
- **Version-control friendly.** Records can be diffed, reviewed and merged exactly like source code, so a community can review each other's work.
- **No lock-in.** Export your data at any time with zero loss.

## 9. How to contribute

Ask a question, report a problem, propose a change, or build something on the standard. You do not need permission for any of it. The [contribute page](/contribute/) has the details; the short version is: open a GitHub Issue using the *Schema Change Proposal* template (problem, proposed change, backward compatibility, examples) or write to maxgen@opengenealogyai.org.

## 10. Governance

MAXGEN is public domain, so anyone can use it, fork it, or extend it. What is stewarded is the canonical version: the one set of files at this address that may be called MAXGEN. Today the author, Garlon Maxwell, is the steward, with a public proposal process (7-day comment for minor changes, 30-day for major) and written decisions. A published charter describes the advisory board that takes over major-version decisions once there are independent adopters, including how it can overrule the steward. What the steward never controls: your forks, your extensions, your tools, or your records. Read the full [governance page](/governance/).

> "MAXGEN is open because anyone can use it and build on it. It is not open to fragmentation. One canonical version. One steward. Every change earns its place in the record." — Garlon Maxwell


---
## The MAXGEN schemas

MAXGEN v2.0 · twelve files, one version
# The schemas

MAXGEN 2.0 is one release: eleven record schemas plus one shared building-blocks file. Every file is JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. All twelve files share one version number, and within 2.x every change is additive: a file valid under 2.0 stays valid under every 2.x.



## Shared building blocks

`maxgen-defs.schema.json` is not a record type: no document is valid against it alone. It holds the parts every record schema uses: ids and small types, the date block, the place block, the evidence link (the part of every claim that says which evidence it rests on), the quote check, saved copies, regions and media pointers, roles and event types, the claim header, the common and lifecycle fields, and the task provenance block. [Download the shared file](/schemas/maxgen/v2/maxgen-defs.schema.json).

## Canonical addresses



Every file declares its own address in its `$id`. A record schema points into the shared file by a relative address, so all twelve files sit side by side in one folder. Validators load all twelve files into one registry and never fetch anything over the network; the addresses do not need to be reachable for validation to work. The fingerprints are also in [SHA256SUMS.txt](/schemas/maxgen/v2/SHA256SUMS.txt), and a machine-readable list of every version is at [`/schemas/maxgen/index.json`](/schemas/maxgen/index.json).

## MAXGEN 1.13 (archived) {#archived-113}

The seven 1.13 schema files stay exactly as they were, at their permanent addresses under `/schemas/maxgen/v1/` and `/schemas/maxgen/v1.NN/`. MAXGEN 2.0 does not read 1.x files. The 1.13 pages are kept for reference: .

## Check a record

Paste any JSON record into the [browser validator](/validator/) to see whether it conforms. Nothing you paste leaves your computer.

## FAQ

Questions and answers
# Frequently asked questions

Grouped by who is asking. If your question is not here, [ask it](/contribute/) and it may be added.

## I'm a genealogist

What is MAXGEN in one sentence?A free, public-domain way of writing down family-history evidence so that every fact keeps its source and an honest confidence score, and conflicting evidence is kept rather than deleted.

Do I need to be technical to benefit from it?No. MAXGEN is what software uses underneath. What you notice is the behaviour: a tree that shows two possible fathers with their scores instead of silently picking one, a search that finds "Makeswell" when you typed "Maxwell", and a document that is never "corrected" away from what the clerk wrote.

Why keep several possible parents? Isn't the job to find the right one?Yes, and keeping the candidates is how you get there honestly. Real research often ends at "probably this man, possibly that one". A format that can hold only one answer has no room for the uncertainty a good genealogist would write in the margin. MAXGEN stores the margin note as data, so a new record can raise one candidate and lower another instead of overturning a false certainty.

What do the confidence numbers mean?They are anchored, not decorative. 0.95 and above means the fact appears verbatim in a source with no ambiguity. 0.70 to 0.95 means well attested with some ambiguity, such as a self-reported census age. 0.50 to 0.70 means plausible but needing more evidence. Below 0.50 is speculative, recorded so it is not lost. Scores must be honest: a consistent 0.4 is more useful than an inflated 0.9.

How does it handle a document that gets the spelling wrong?The document record (MaxRecord) keeps the spelling exactly as written. The interpretation ("that is the Maxwell family") lives separately in the person record, with a score and a source. And the name record (MaxName) can state, with citations, that Makeswell is a known variant of Maxwell in Scots records between 1600 and 1750, so searches find it.

Will my existing GEDCOM files work?MAXGEN is not a replacement for GEDCOM as a way to move a finished tree between programs. It is a way to exchange the evidence and reasoning behind a tree. Its event types map to GEDCOM tags, so conversion tools can go in both directions; the difference is that a MAXGEN record can say "we are 0.6 sure" and a GEDCOM record cannot.

What about living relatives?A record about a person who may be alive is locked private by the schema itself: public systems answer "not found". DNA records are always private and can never hold raw genetic data. Research tasks about living people can never be sent to outside volunteers or third-party AI services. These are rules of the standard, not settings an application can turn off.

Can AI make things up in a MAXGEN record?It can try, and the standard is built to catch it. Every claim must cite a source record. Every research task lists the evidence it must return (a link to the actual birth record, the exact search used). Results are reviewed by someone other than the contributor, and "fabricated or hallucinated" is a formal rejection reason that lowers a contributor's standing over time.

Does it cost anything?No. The standard is dedicated to the public domain (CC0): use it for anything, including commercial products, with no conditions. The schemas, the specification, and the podcasts on this site cost nothing.

## I'm a developer

What format is it?JSON, described by JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). Seven schema files, one per record type, all at the same version number. Records are plain JSON documents; the conventional file extensions are .maxgen for persons and .mxrecord for source documents, but any JSON file that validates is a MAXGEN record.

Where do I get the schema files?At their canonical addresses, which are also each file's $id: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v1/&lt;name&gt;.schema.json. Frozen copies of every release live under /schemas/maxgen/v1.NN/. See the schemas page and versions.

How do I validate a record?Any JSON Schema 2020-12 validator works: Ajv in JavaScript, jsonschema in Python, and equivalents in other languages. The schema repository ships validators and fixtures. Or paste a record into the browser validator on this site.

Can I add my own fields?Yes, in extensions{}, which every schema has and which accepts anything. The core of each schema is closed (unknown top-level fields are rejected) so validation is exact; the extensions object is open so you never need to fork. Your records stay valid across releases.

Will an update break my records?Not within a major version. Minor releases are additive only: new optional fields, new enum values, loosened constraints. Fields are never renamed or removed in v1.x. A breaking change means v2, a new address space, a migration guide, and a 30-day public comment period first. Read the stability promise.

Why is one version number shared by all seven schemas?So there is never any doubt about which files go together. When any schema changes, all seven are stamped with the new number and released as a set. It is the model HL7 FHIR and GEDCOM use. Before v1.3 the schemas versioned independently and the skew was confusing; lockstep ended that.

Which fields are required?Few, deliberately. A MaxPerson needs an ID, at least one name assertion, and who asserted it and when. A MaxRecord needs an ID, a record type, a licence, a source URL, an extraction confidence and the living flag. Each schema page lists its fields with the required ones marked.

What are the normative rules I must implement?Three. A record with is_living: true is tier2-private and must not be exposed publicly. MaxDNA records are always tier2-private and raw_genotype_stored is always false. MaxTask contributor_eligibility defaults to first_party_only and any task about a living person must stay that way.

How are confidence scores combined?The schemas store the evidence; the engine does the arithmetic. The reference approach is a noisy-OR combination weighted by source quality, which raises confidence when independent sources agree without ever reaching certainty. Because every assertion cites its source_record_id, an engine can detect two assertions that really come from one document and avoid double-counting.

Is there an official library or package?Not yet. The schema repository contains JavaScript validators and fixtures. Packages for npm and PyPI are planned after launch; if you publish one, tell us and it will be listed.

How do I propose a change?Open a GitHub Issue with the problem, the proposed fields, the backward-compatibility answer and a before-and-after example. Minor changes get at least a week of open discussion, major ones a month, then a written decision. Details on the governance page.

## I run an archive, library or society

What would adopting MAXGEN commit us to?Only to publishing records that validate against the public schemas and to honouring the three privacy rules. There is no membership, no fee, no agreement to sign, and no obligation to use the whole standard: an archive that only wants to publish transcriptions with provenance can use MaxRecognition alone.

Who owns the standard?Nobody, legally: it is dedicated to the public domain under CC0, so anyone may use, copy, change and redistribute it with no conditions. The canonical version is stewarded by its author today, with a published path to an advisory board that includes an archive or library seat and can overrule the steward on major versions by a two-thirds vote. See governance.

Can we keep our own catalogue numbers and internal fields?Yes. MaxRecord has archive_ref for your reference, repository and collection for where the item sits, and extensions{} for anything else. MaxSource's access{} block records how you want to be accessed, including crawl etiquette that robots.txt cannot express.

How does it handle attribution and licensing of our records?Every record declares its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, or never-redistribute) and carries an attribution{} object for the credit line your licence requires. The standard itself is public domain; your data stays under whatever terms you set.

We have transcriptions made by volunteers over decades. Is that work preserved?That is what MaxRecognition is for. Each transcription gets a provenance record: who read it, their credentials and specialties, how confident they were word by word, and which readings were direct and which were inferred. The work becomes citable and its quality trackable, instead of being flattened into a text field.

## About the project

Why is it called MAXGEN?It stands for the Maxwell Genealogy Standard, after its author Garlon Maxwell. The name is a mark for the canonical version: use it for anything that validates against the public schemas, but not for a fork that diverges.

What is OpenGenealogyAI, and what is The Probable Pedigree?OpenGenealogyAI is the organisation that stewards MAXGEN. The Probable Pedigree is a genealogy platform built on the standard that shows what it makes possible. The standard is designed to outlive any product, including that one: it has no special standing in the change process.

Why seven schemas instead of one?Because evidence, interpretation, work, names, sources, transcription and DNA are different things with different privacy needs and different owners. Separating them lets a document be re-read without touching conclusions, lets DNA be locked down harder than everything else, and lets an organisation adopt only the layer it needs.

Who made the podcasts?They were produced with an AI narration tool from scripts written by the standard's author and describe MAXGEN v1.11. Where a later release changed a detail, the schema pages on this site are authoritative.

How does this relate to FamilySearch, Ancestry, WikiTree and the other sites?They hold the records and the communities; MAXGEN is a format for describing evidence that any of them, and any tool built around them, could read and write. It is not a competing service and it does not replace anyone's database. A MaxPerson can carry scored links to the same person on FamilySearch, WikiTree or Find a Grave, so research done in different places can be reconciled instead of duplicated. The aim is a shared language, and the more sites speak it the more useful everyone's work becomes.

Is MAXGEN trying to replace GEDCOM?No. GEDCOM moves finished trees between programs and has done so for forty years. MAXGEN carries the evidence and reasoning behind a tree, which GEDCOM was never designed to hold. Event types map to GEDCOM tags so conversion runs both ways, and a tool can happily support both.

How do I follow changes?Every release is recorded in the changelog with the reason it happened. Proposals are discussed in public on GitHub. A mailing list is planned.


---
## Versions

Releases · current v2.0
# Versions and the stability promise

## How versions work

**One version number for all twelve files.** The eleven record schemas and the shared building-blocks file are released together as one MAXGEN version, so you adopt "MAXGEN 2.0" as a set and never have to wonder which file goes with which. Every document carries `schema_version`, and the 2.x schemas accept any `"2."` stamp (`"2.0"`, `"2.1"` and so on; not `"2.01"`, not `"1.13"`).

## The 2.x promise

> **Within 2.x, every change is additive:** a new optional property, a new value in a list, a new shared definition in `maxgen-defs.schema.json` (a `$defs` entry), a new record schema file, or a loosened limit. **Never:** removing or renaming a property, making an optional property required, narrowing a pattern, range or list, or changing what a value means. A file valid under 2.0 stays valid under every 2.x.

- **Files keep the stamp they were written with.** There is no re-stamping of old files at each release.
- **Unknown values fall back safely.** A reader that meets a list value it does not know reads a vocabulary word as `other` and shows the words as written; a state that software manages fails closed (an unknown licence is read as `tier2-private`).
- **A major version** (`v2` → `v3`) means breaking changes and a new `$id` address space.

## What 2.0 changed

MAXGEN 2.0 is the first major version. It reshaped the seven 1.x schemas, added four new ones (MaxRelationship, MaxPlace, MaxGroup and MaxEvent) and a shared building-blocks file, and moved family links out of MaxPerson into MaxRelationship, where each link is stored once. **2.0 does not read 1.x files, and there is no migration from 1.x.** The 1.x files are not deleted: they stay at their permanent addresses, unchanged. The [changelog](/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16) lists what changed in every schema and what breaks.

## Permanent addresses

- `/schemas/maxgen/v2/` holds the **current 2.x files**. This is the `$id` inside every 2.0 file.
- `/schemas/maxgen/v2.0/` is a **frozen copy** of the 2.0 release.
- `/schemas/maxgen/v1/.schema.json` and `/schemas/maxgen/v1.NN/.schema.json` hold the **archived 1.x releases**, unchanged.
- `/schemas/maxgen/index.json` lists every version, with each 2.0 file's SHA-256, for machines.



## Changelog

Every release, what changed in each schema and why, is on the [changelog page](/changelog/).


---
## Governance

How the standard changes
# Governance

MAXGEN is dedicated to the public domain (CC0). Anyone can use it, fork it, extend it, or build on it without asking. What is stewarded is the **canonical version**: the one set of files at `opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/` that may be called MAXGEN. This page says who decides what goes into it, how, and how that will change as the community grows.

> "MAXGEN is open because anyone can use it and build on it. It is not open to fragmentation. One canonical version. One steward. Every change earns its place in the record." — Garlon Maxwell

## Today: a steward

The standard's author, Garlon Maxwell, is the steward: the technical lead who has final say on what enters the canonical schemas until the advisory board exists. Every decision is public, reasoned, and recorded in the [changelog](/versions/#changelog). This is the same arrangement most successful standards began with, including the OpenAPI specification before it moved to a foundation, and the page below says exactly when and how it ends.

## How to propose a change

1. **Open a GitHub Issue** in the schema repository using the *Schema Change Proposal* template. It asks four things:
    - **Problem**: what real use the current schema fails to support.
    - **Proposed change**: the new or altered fields, with type and description.
    - **Backward compatibility**: does any existing valid record become invalid? If so, how would it migrate?
    - **Examples**: at least one before-and-after JSON snippet.
2. **Open discussion.** Anyone may comment. Minor (additive) changes stay open at least **7 days**; major (breaking) changes at least **30 days**.
3. **Review.** The steward reads the proposal and the discussion, may ask for more examples, and may put the question to a wider vote.
4. **Decision with reasons.** Accepted or declined, in writing, on the issue. Nothing merges without explicit sign-off.
5. **Implementation.** The change is applied to the schema files, fixtures are re-validated, the changelog is written, and a new version is released under the [versioning policy](/versions/).

Challenges that did **not** lead to a change are logged too. A rule that survived a good argument is worth knowing about.

If you do not use GitHub, write to **maxgen@opengenealogyai.org** and the steward will open the issue on your behalf.

## Tomorrow: an advisory board

A standard controlled by one person is a standard institutions hesitate to adopt. The path to shared control is published now so that adopters can see it.

**Trigger.** The board convenes when there are three or more independent implementations of MAXGEN, or when the first institution (an archive, a library, a genealogical society, a software vendor) adopts it, whichever comes first.

**Composition.** Five to seven seats: the steward, working genealogists, developers who have shipped an implementation, and at least one representative of an archive or library. No single company may hold a majority.

**What the board decides.** Major versions, additions to the core schemas, and changes to the normative privacy rules. Extensions need nobody's permission and are never voted on.

**What the steward keeps.** A tie-breaking vote and custody of the name and the canonical address. The steward may be **overruled on a major version by a two-thirds vote**. That clause is the point: it is the guarantee that the standard cannot be held hostage by its author.

**Openness.** Meetings are announced in advance, minutes are published on this site, and every vote is recorded.

**How seats are filled.** The first board is appointed by the steward from people who have actually implemented or adopted MAXGEN, announced publicly with a 30-day objection period. After that, seats are two-year terms; the sitting board fills vacancies by simple majority from public nominations. Anyone may nominate anyone, including themselves.

**Quorum and voting.** A quorum is a majority of seats. Additive changes pass by simple majority of those voting. Major versions and changes to the privacy rules need two-thirds of all seats. Every vote is recorded with names.

**Emergency fixes.** A security or privacy defect in a schema may be patched immediately by the steward as a patch release, with a public notice the same day and retrospective board review within 30 days. Nothing else skips the process.

## Continuity: what happens if the steward is gone

A standard that dies with one person is not a standard. Three safeguards:

1. **The licence is CC0.** Nobody needs permission to carry on. If the canonical site went dark, every schema file and this whole site could be republished by anyone, from the public git history, the same day.
2. **A named successor.** The steward keeps a named successor on file with the board (or, before the board exists, publicly in the repository). If the steward is unreachable for 90 days, the successor, or the board by majority, assumes stewardship and the name.
3. **Frozen releases.** Every version is archived at a permanent address, so an adopter never depends on the steward being available to fetch the files they validated against.

## What the steward does not control

- Private forks and extensions. Add fields in `extensions{}` or fork the files outright. No permission needed.
- Tools built on MAXGEN. Commercial or free, open or closed.
- Records you publish in MAXGEN format.
- Proposals. All are welcome and all get an answer.

What you may not do is call a diverging fork "MAXGEN". The name means the canonical version.

## Conflict of interest

The steward's own genealogy platform, The Probable Pedigree, implements MAXGEN. It gets no special treatment: its change requests go through the same public process, and anything specific to its business (pricing, payments, accounts) stays in `extensions{}` and never enters the standard. The MaxTask schema deliberately contains no payment fields for exactly this reason.

## Contribute

Get involved
# Contribute

## Ask a question

- **GitHub Discussions** on the [OpenGenealogyAI organisation](https://github.com/OpenGenealogyai): free to read, free account to post. Questions that keep coming up are promoted into the [FAQ](/faq/).
- **Email**: maxgen@opengenealogyai.org, for anyone who would rather not use GitHub.

## Report a problem

Found a record that should validate but does not, a description that contradicts the field, or a fixture that is wrong? Open an issue in the schema repository with the JSON that shows it. A reproducible example is worth more than a paragraph.

## Propose a change

Follow the process on the [governance page](/governance/): problem, proposed change, backward compatibility, examples. Additive proposals that come with a fixture are the easiest to accept.

## Build on it

You do not need permission. Some useful starting points:

- Validate records against the canonical schemas at `https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v1/`, or try the [browser validator](/validator/).
- Keep your own fields in `extensions{}` so your records stay valid across releases.
- Honour the three normative rules: living people stay private, DNA stays private and never holds raw genotypes, and tasks about living people are never sent outside.
- Tell us. Implementations are listed on this site, and three independent ones convene the advisory board.

## Help with the content

The FAQ and the schema pages are all improvable. Corrections and clearer wording are welcome as issues or pull requests against the website repository.

## Licence

# Licence

## The standard: CC0

The seven MAXGEN schema files and the text of the standard on this site are dedicated to the public domain under the [Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) dedication. You may copy, change, redistribute and build on them for any purpose, commercial or not, without asking and without attribution.

Why CC0 rather than a licence that requires credit? Because a standard only works when adopting it costs nothing, legally or administratively. An archive's counsel should be able to approve MAXGEN in one reading. Credit is welcome, never required.

### If you want to credit us anyway

- In software or documentation: *"Uses the MAXGEN standard by OpenGenealogyAI (opengenealogyai.org)."*
- In a dataset: the `schema_version` field and the `$id` reference to `opengenealogyai.org` in every MAXGEN record already say where it came from.
- In a paper or article: cite as shown at the bottom of this page.

## Records: each carries its own

Every record written in MAXGEN declares its own `redistribution_license`: `CC0`, `public-domain`, `CC-BY`, `CC-BY-SA`, or `tier2-private` (never redistribute). Where a source requires attribution, the `attribution{}` object in the record holds the credit. The standard is public domain; the data written in it is whatever its owner says it is.

## Code: MIT

The validators, fixtures and tooling in the schema repository are released under the [MIT licence](https://opensource.org/license/mit).

## Names and logo

"MAXGEN", "OpenGenealogyAI" and the star-tree logo identify the canonical standard and its steward. Use them to say your software implements MAXGEN. Do not use them for a fork that diverges from the canonical schemas, and do not imply that OpenGenealogyAI endorses your product unless it does.

## How to cite

> Maxwell, G. *MAXGEN: The Maxwell Genealogy Standard*, version 2.0. OpenGenealogyAI. https://opengenealogyai.org/ — CC0 1.0.

# The MAXGEN podcast

Each of the seven original schemas gets one conversation. Start with the overview if you are new, or jump to the schema you care about.

Subscribe in any podcast app with the feed address **`https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/feed.xml`**.

These episodes were produced with an AI narration tool from written scripts by the standard's author, and describe MAXGEN v1.11. MAXGEN 2.0 changed a great deal since, so each episode links to what changed. Where an episode and a schema page disagree, the schema page is authoritative. The four schemas new in 2.0 (MaxRelationship, MaxPlace, MaxGroup and MaxEvent) have no episode yet.

## MaxRecord (MAXGEN 2.0 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxrecord/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/raw-record.schema.json  SHA-256 14b1cc31cdfda239d90d0e6e7b49dcbf27a6c3b28581c1d9ccf8ae1bdac27760
One MaxRecord is one document, copied word for word.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxRecord is one original document (or one copy of it), copied word for word with every person it names and every event it records, so that one original equals one record.

### Fields

- record_id (uuid, required): This record's permanent random id, created once by the writer and never recomputed or reused.
- record_type (enum, required): What kind of document this is; census_household holds a whole household, gazetteer_entry is an authored gazetteer or authority page, and dna_match_list is always tier2-private and living.
- record_type_as_written (string): The document's or program's own words for its type, used with other.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this record may be shared, and under what licence; must be tier2-private while is_living_flag is true.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A: whether anyone this record names may be alive (unsure means true); true requires tier2-private, it is a floor that only rises, and privacy is always worked out again when read.
- source_classification (source_classification, required): Whether the document is an original, a copy or an authored work, and how first-hand its information is overall.
- transcription_parts (array of transcription_part): The document's text word for word, in labelled parts; a line that starts with [label] and one space carries that line label.
- transcription_scope (enum): How much of the document was transcribed; only complete_entry or complete_list can carry evidence of absence; required when transcription_parts is present.
- transcription_sha256 (sha256): Helper-owned fingerprint of transcription_parts in canonical form, used to tell when quote checks are stale.
- extraction_confidence (confidence): How faithfully the transcription follows the document, from 0 to 1; required when transcription_parts is present.
- persons_mentioned (array of mention): Every person the document names, one mention each, as written.
- events_documented (array of event_entry): The events this document records, one entry each (one per child for twins); the helper gives each entry its own occurrence.
- record_date (date): The date the entry or document was written, not the date of the event it records.
- record_place (place_ref): Where the document was made, as written.
- record_status (enum): Whether this is the first issue of the document or an amended, delayed or reissued one; lineage facts citing an amended, delayed or reissued record are flagged for review (R-18).
- record_status_as_written (string): The document's own words for its status, used with other.
- copied_from (array of copy_step): The step back toward the original that this copy was made from; required with at least one step when the source is derivative, and the full chain is found by following record ids, never copied here.
- part_of_source_id (uuid): The MaxSource (collection, book, film) this record belongs to; containment, kept apart from copying.
- repository_as_written (string): The archive, library or family holding the document, as written.
- collection_as_written (string): The collection the document sits in, as written.
- locator (locator): Where the document sits in its collection: volume, page, line and so on.
- original_key (original_key): Helper-built stable name of the original document, used to refuse duplicates and to judge independence; never written by hand.
- source_url (uri): The web address where the document was read; optional, and never invented.
- citation_as_written (string): A footnote or citation string exactly as another program or publication gave it.
- citation_template (citation_template): A citation template another program used for this document, with its field values.
- saved_copies (array of saved_copy): The files this record captured, each described here once and keyed by fingerprint; frozen once stored apart from their descriptive fields.
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Files described on another record that this record also uses.
- attribution (attribution): Credit for the human who photographed, transcribed or compiled this record; a credit never sets a living flag.
- rights_uri (uri): A web address stating the rights in this document.
- sensitive_data_redacted (boolean): True when sensitive details (identity numbers, medical details) were left out of the transcription.
- redaction_notes (string): What was left out and why.
- archive_ref (string): A local path where this record is kept; private, never exported.

### Example (made up; marriage_register_1880_obadiah_patience.json)

```json
{
  "record_id": "71642fb1-7db2-5581-8a08-cb4df77ea03e",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "record_type": "marriage_register",
  "redistribution_license": "public-domain",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "source_classification": {
    "source": "original",
    "information": "primary"
  },
  "transcription_parts": [
    {
      "part_id": "p1",
      "lang": "en",
      "text": "[4] 1 May 1880 | Obadiah Mossbury, bachelor | Patience Wren, spinster"
    }
  ],
  "transcription_scope": "complete_entry",
  "extraction_confidence": 0.95,
  "persons_mentioned": [
    {
      "mention_id": "m1",
      "name_as_written": "Obadiah Mossbury",
      "role_as_written": "groom",
      "role": "groom",
      "in_event_refs": [
        "e1"
      ],
      "lines": [
        "4"
      ],
      "is_living": false
    },
    {
      "mention_id": "m2",
      "name_as_written": "Patience Wren",
      "role_as_written": "bride",
      "role": "bride",
      "in_event_refs": [
        "e1"
      ],
      "lines": [
        "4"
      ],
      "is_living": false
    }
  ],
  "events_documented": [
    {
      "ref": "e1",
      "event_type": "marriage",
      "is_primary": true,
      "date": {
        "value": {
          "year": 1880,
          "month": 5,
          "day": 1
        },
        "as_written": "1 May 1880"
      },
      "place": {
        "place_as_written": "St Wren's, Tumblebrook"
      },
      "information": "primary"
    }
  ],
  "part_of_source_id": "75df6185-5f2f-5652-afb4-fb6349ea015f",
  "locator": {
    "as_written": "Tumblebrook marriages, entry 4",
    "register": "marriages",
    "entry": "4"
  },
  "created_by_task_id": "f29d3707-1833-510d-ae04-a2304e60a471",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

One original, one record, holding the whole entry. `transcription` becomes
`transcription_parts` with permanent line labels, `transcription_scope` (complete entry,
complete list, partial) and a kit-computed fingerprint. Added: `persons_mentioned` with a
permanent `mention_id`, the page's own role words and `is_living` for every person;
`events_documented`, the events the document records, each with `information` judged per event
(each gets an occasion id); `source_classification` as a required core field (it was under
`extensions`); `copied_from` (the copying chain, required for a derivative); `part_of_source_id`
and `locator`; a kit-built `original_key` that refuses a second copy of the same original;
`record_status` (amended, delayed, reissued); `saved_copies` and `media_refs`;
`citation_as_written` and `citation_template`. `source_url` becomes optional, but "where it is"
is required (an address, a saved copy, or a repository or source with a locator; never an
invented URL). `record_date` is the date the entry was written. `census_row` is renamed
`census_household`; new types include `birth_register`, `death_register`, `tree_import`,
`gazetteer_entry` and `dna_match_list`. Removed: `transcription`, `image_url`, `locations`,
`repository`, `collection` (now `_as_written` fields), `language`, `alternate_names`,
`digital_object_id`, `extracted_by`, `extracted_at`.

### Listen

Episode 1, MaxRecord — Source documents as written (25:40): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-01-maxrecord.mp3 — Evidence versus interpretation, and why the clerk who wrote 'Makeswell' must never be corrected. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxPerson (MAXGEN 2.0 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxperson/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/person.schema.json  SHA-256 280f09fbee28e3048dd443ff8dee5ec4d12449b2eada4dd4470df2945b582ac6
One MaxPerson is one person, as a researched conclusion (holds no family links).

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxPerson is one person as a researched conclusion, every fact about them a claim citing one piece of evidence, holding no family links (parents, children and partners live in MaxRelationship).

### Fields

- person_id (uuid, required): This person's permanent random id, created once by the writer and never recomputed or reused.
- person_kind (enum): Whether this is a documented person or a placeholder made only so something (a parent link, a DNA hypothesis, a death) can attach to them; never created under an import task (R-23).
- placeholder_label (string): Plain words saying who a placeholder stands for, such as "unknown father of Mabel's three daughters"; required when person_kind is placeholder.
- is_living (boolean, required): Living A: whether this person may be alive, with no default (unsure means true); true requires tier2-private, it is a floor that only rises, and privacy is always worked out again when read.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this person's document may be shared, and under what licence; must be tier2-private while is_living is true.
- outside_ids: refused by name (a document that contains it is not valid)
- name_assertions (array of name_claim): Name claims, each citing its evidence; at least one is required unless person_kind is placeholder.
- gender_assertions (array of gender_claim): Gender claims, each keeping the document's own words.
- birth_assertions (array of vital_claim): Claims about this person's own birth, always with role principal (another person's part at a birth goes in event_assertions).
- death_assertions (array of death_claim): Claims about this person's own death, always with role principal (another person's part at a death goes in event_assertions).
- event_assertions (array of event_claim): Other events in this person's life and their roles at other people's events; a couple event with role principal, bride, groom, spouse or partner is refused here because it is a family fact written with link (R-22).
- attribute_assertions (array of attribute_claim): Lasting facts such as occupation, residence or religion, each citing its evidence.
- non_event_assertions (array of non_event_claim): Claims that something did not happen, such as no marriage by a stated date (GEDCOM 7 NO).
- membership_assertions (array of membership_claim): Membership of a historical group, each citing this person's own line on a roster or similar record (MaxGroup keeps no member list).
- photo_assertions (array of photo_claim): Claims that a face or figure on a photograph record is this person.
- external_id_assertions (array of external_id_claim): Claims that this person is the same as a profile in another system; the only place an outside id for a person is recorded.
- attached_sources (array of attached_source): Records another program attached to this person without naming a fact; research pointers only, never evidence.
- same_as_candidates (array of same_as_candidate): People who may be the same as this one but are not merged (GEDCOM 7 ALIA); a merge still needs the merge_person path.

### Example (made up; birth_calculated_from_census_age.json)

```json
{
  "person_id": "2a946e38-5769-5fdc-b888-e67cc4b40342",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "is_living": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "name_assertions": [
    {
      "name_as_written": "Mossbury, Amos",
      "given_name": "Amos",
      "surname": "Mossbury",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Mossbury, Amos",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "birth_assertions": [
    {
      "date": {
        "modifier": "about",
        "value": {
          "year": 1896
        },
        "derivation": "calculated",
        "derivation_note": "age 44 on the 1940 census day"
      },
      "age_as_written": "44",
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Mossbury, Amos | Head | M | 44",
        "kind": "indirect"
      }
    }
  ],
  "attribute_assertions": [
    {
      "attribute_type": "occupation",
      "value_as_written": "Miller",
      "occurrence_id": "8a37321b-3688-589b-8d1a-1a596a352edb",
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "325d904c-1f07-52ff-85d2-856cb65a60cd",
        "mention_id": "11",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Miller",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "f1f1f427-edc8-59ac-b068-c44d0daf5f82",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

**Holds no family links.** Removed: `parent_assertions`, `child_assertions`,
`spouse_assertions` (to MaxRelationship); `composite_confidence` (a stored score);
`external_ids` (a mirror); `dna_evidence` (DNA is cited through the evidence link);
`place_registry` (to MaxPlace); `source_record_ids` (an index); `occupation_assertions` (now
`attribute_assertions` with `attribute_type: occupation`); `asserted_by`, `asserted_at`,
`last_updated_at`, `judge_approved`, `judge_approved_at` (task provenance, kit timestamps and
the database's review stage); `merge_status` (now `lifecycle`); the flat date keys and
`country_code`/`state_province` (now the date and place blocks). Changed: every claim gains the
claim header and an evidence link; photo claims point at a photograph record. Added:
`person_kind` and `placeholder_label`, attribute, non-event and group-membership claims,
`name_parts` and `name_status`, `attached_sources`, `same_as_candidates`. `is_living` and
`redistribution_license` become required, with no default; `name_assertions` is required for a
documented person.

### Listen

Episode 2, MaxPerson — The person who might be your ancestor (22:46): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-02-maxperson-v2.mp3 — Assertions not facts, probabilistic parents, composite confidence, and the merge model. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxRelationship (MAXGEN 2.0 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxrelationship/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/relationship.schema.json  SHA-256 3fe0a82b950eb6fa5b501258cf50c9b41894f7f41039051a16170cc5c5af5d5d
One MaxRelationship is one family link, stored once: a `family`, a `parent_child` pair or an `association`.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one family link stored once: a family (a union, household or parent set with its child memberships), one parent and child pair with its lineage facts, or a standing association between two people. Agents never write these files by hand: the helper's link command finds or creates them, and only import_file, resolve_conflict and build_tree tasks may add one directly (R-24). MaxPerson keeps no copy of any link and there is no two-sided lock.

### Fields

- relationship_id (uuid, required): This link's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the helper's link command (or by the importer or analysis task that adds it), never computed from the people's ids and never reused.
- kind (enum, required): Which of the three kinds of link this document is (family, parent_child or association); each kind forbids the other kinds' fields, and a document of an unknown kind is refused at write and skipped with a warning at read
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor, required with no default: true when a person this link names may be alive (a family: either partner only, since each child is judged on its own membership; a parent_child record: the parent or the child; 
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Licence of this link, set by the helper to the strictest of the people it names and the records its claims cite (a family: the partners and the records its family facts cite) and raised later but never lowered; a true is
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Photographs of the couple or the family, pointing at saved copies that are described once on the records that captured them.
- partners (array of partner): Family only: zero to two live partner items, unordered, each either a person or an absent partner whom a document mentions without naming; absent and person items both count toward the two, retracted items stay stored an
- union_type (enum): Family only: the importing program's (or the writer's) word for the kind of union, kept as given, unknown when nothing says; never shown when the family has live family facts, which are the only evidence of a union; shar
- union_type_as_written (string): Family only: the documents' or the other program's own words for the union, kept when union_type is other or when the words say more.
- union_type_uri (uri): Family only: a published vocabulary's address for the union type, when one exists.
- fact_assertions (array of family_fact_claim): Family only: facts about the couple or household (marriage, banns, licence, divorce, a census showing them as husband and wife ...), each one claim citing one piece of evidence and held by the partner set.
- non_event_assertions (array of non_event_claim): Family only: things the evidence says did not happen to this couple (GEDCOM 7 NO), each one claim with the same shape as MaxPerson's; an undated one never counts toward the living test or date bounds.
- children (array of membership): Family only: each child's place in this parent set; a child may hold two memberships in one family only when their set kinds differ, because there is one live membership per child, family and set kind (R-20).
- parent_id (uuid): Parent_child only: the parent person, resolved through merge redirects when read; there is exactly one live parent_child record per parent and child pair (R-20).
- child_id (uuid): Parent_child only: the child person, resolved through merge redirects when read; it must differ from parent_id (R-06).
- parent_role (enum): Parent_child only: the parent's role as the documents show it, unknown until a document says; a later father-versus-mother conflict is refused by the helper for an analysis task to settle.
- parent_role_as_written (string): Parent_child only: the parent's own words on the record, such as Head or father, never the child's words.
- lineage_assertions (array of lineage_claim): Parent_child only: at least one lineage fact saying what kind of parent this person is to this child, each judged on its own evidence; one man who is both birth father and adoptive father has one record holding two facts
- association_type (enum): Association only: the kind of standing tie, with this direction: godparent -- party1 is the godparent; enslaved_by -- party1 is the enslaved person and party2 the enslaver; ancestor_descendant -- party1 is the ancestor; 
- association_type_as_written (string): Association only: the document's or the other program's own words for the tie, kept when association_type is other or when the words say more.
- association_type_uri (uri): Association only: a published vocabulary's address for the association type, when one exists.
- generations (integer): Association only, and only with association_type ancestor_descendant: how many generations separate party1 (the ancestor) from party2, when known.
- party1 (party): Association only: the first party; for a directed type it is the godparent, the enslaved person, the ancestor or the employer.
- party2 (party): Association only: the second party; for a directed type it is the godchild, the enslaver, the descendant or the employee.
- association_assertions (array of association_claim): Association only: at least one claim that the tie existed, began or ended, each citing one piece of evidence.

### Example (made up; parent_child_candidate_father_a.json)

```json
{
  "relationship_id": "c967855d-e512-5c3c-8084-aa1c3439e312",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "kind": "parent_child",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "parent_id": "fed1f33a-d9b4-51f2-9d73-d97aee90c2b4",
  "child_id": "65feecf1-edc0-53b0-8a07-facdedecc81b",
  "parent_role": "father",
  "parent_role_as_written": "reputed father",
  "lineage_assertions": [
    {
      "assertion_id": "7d437c4d-f926-5e5d-907f-d8240e0c8b20",
      "fact_type": "birth_parent",
      "parent_mention_id": "m3",
      "child_mention_id": "m1",
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "task_id": "321dd029-e1b0-5335-814f-37fd6711f5bb",
      "evidence": {
        "basis": "document",
        "source_record_id": "cbbbabf3-db47-51a4-8001-88c4e784c88a",
        "mention_id": "m1",
        "record_event_ref": "e1",
        "quote": "Pip, base son of Dorcas Bramblecott, singlewoman; reputed father Ned Mossbury",
        "kind": "direct"
      }
    }
  ],
  "created_by_task_id": "321dd029-e1b0-5335-814f-37fd6711f5bb",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

Every family link, stored once. Three kinds: **`family`** (0 to 2 partners — a person, or an
"absent" partner the document mentions without naming — family facts such as marriage, banns,
divorce or a census together, and child memberships, each with a `set_kind`: `birth`,
`adoptive`, `step_household`, `foster`, `guardianship`, `sealing`, `alternative_hypothesis`,
`other`, a `child_order` and a kit-computed `is_preferred`); **`parent_child`** (one per parent
and child, with lineage facts such as `birth_parent`, `adoptive_parent`, `step_parent`, each
with a dimension: genetic, gestational, legal, social, religious, household, unknown, other); and
**`association`** (godparent, enslaved by, ancestor-descendant, employer, neighbour, friend,
multiple birth, other). No two-sided lock: MaxPerson keeps no copy of any link. A child can belong to
several parent sets, so an adopted person can trace both their birth and their adoptive
lineage. Agents never write these files: the kit's `link` command finds or makes them. Replaces
1.13's `parent_assertions`, `child_assertions`, `spouse_assertions`, `relationship_type` on
parents and the `ecclesiastical` type.

### Listen

No episode yet: MaxRelationship is new in MAXGEN 2.0.


---
## MaxTask (MAXGEN 2.0 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxtask/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/task-queue.schema.json  SHA-256 f636aebfa334a37021ec4b5f1ebc9b41ab61c4cdfc0cde5200fb112686005b6c
One MaxTask is one piece of work: research, an import, a review or a proof.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxTask is the permanent record of one piece of work done in a database (research, an import, a review or a proof), never pruned while anything points at it.

### Fields

- task_id (uuid, required): This task's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.
- created_by_task_id: refused by name (a document that contains it is not valid)
- task_type (enum, required): What kind of work this is; a task of type other permits none of the gated actions of rules R-24, R-28 and R-31.
- task_type_as_written (string): The kind of work in the writer's own words, given when task_type is other.
- status (enum, required): Where the work stands, changed only through the helper's task command (pending, processing, then done, failed or escalated; on_hold pauses it; a task made by mistake or retracted is cancelled, never deleted).
- priority (integer): How urgent the task is, from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest).
- payload (object): The task's input, an open object whose documented kinds are interview, person_request, person_page_session, fan_survey (person_id), run (run_id, on a judge_review task), find_original (record_id), import_file (format: ge
- result (result): What the work found and decided, in a closed, readable shape.
- provenance (provenance): Helper-owned and written once: who did the work of this task, filled when the task is first claimed (moved to processing) or created already done.
- created_by (string): The agent id of the session that wrote this task: optional in input, filled by the helper from the writing session, required in stored form, and a different value is refused (R-14).
- started_at (timestamp): Helper-owned: when the task was first moved to processing.
- completed_at (timestamp): Helper-owned: when the task reached done, failed or cancelled.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor: true when the task names or concerns someone who may be alive (unsure means true); it only rises, and while it is true the task must be first_party_only.
- contributor_eligibility (enum): Who may be given this task: first_party_only (the person's own kit and agents, the default, failing closed) or any_contributor; it must be first_party_only whenever is_living_flag is true.
- assigned_to (string): The agent id now working on this task; absent while it is pending.
- cost_usd (number): What the work actually cost, in US dollars.
- cost_cap_usd (number): The most this task may cost, in US dollars; the agent stops and escalates before going over it.
- retry_count (integer): How many times the task has been retried after a failure.
- max_retries (integer): How many retries are allowed before the task is left failed.
- error_message (string): What went wrong, when the task failed or was escalated.
- escalation_reason (string): Why the task was escalated for a further decision.
- queue_file_path (string): The task's path in a file-based queue on this computer; private, never exported.
- depends_on (array of uuid): Tasks that must be done before this one can start.
- parent_task_id (uuid): The task that made this task (on MaxTask this replaces created_by_task_id, which tasks may not carry).
- acceptance_criteria (array of string): Plain, checkable conditions that a complete result must meet.
- min_confidence (confidence): The lowest result confidence that can be accepted.
- evidence_required (array of string): What the worker must hand back as proof of the work (addresses, exact queries, records saved).
- deadline (timestamp): When the work should be finished.

### Example (made up; extract_record_with_steps.json)

```json
{
  "task_id": "79f310ff-0478-5af4-abc5-f6316de4cffb",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "task_type": "extract_record",
  "status": "done",
  "payload": {
    "kind": "extract",
    "person_id": "0aacaa81-8ca0-5df6-8ff8-2a9f7067d76f"
  },
  "result": {
    "hypothesis_tested": "Mabel was baptised at Tumblebrook in 1924.",
    "what_we_did_and_result": "Searched two collections; found the baptism entry; one site needed a login.",
    "steps": [
      {
        "step_no": 1,
        "action": "search",
        "source": "Tumblebrook parish registers (made-up online images)",
        "source_id": "75df6185-5f2f-5652-afb4-fb6349ea015f",
        "source_url": "https://records.example.org/sample/tumblebrook-baptisms",
        "query": "Thistlewood baptisms 1920-1930",
        "coverage": {
          "span": {
            "modifier": "from_to",
            "value": {
              "year": 1920
            },
            "value2": {
              "year": 1930
            },
            "derivation": "interpreted"
          },
          "place": {
            "place_as_written": "Tumblebrook"
          },
          "record_types": [
            "parish_register"
          ]
        },
        "found": "one entry: Mabel, baptised 16 March 1924",
        "record_id": "d990b9d1-f418-573b-83e7-21792a44085d",
        "person_id": "0aacaa81-8ca0-5df6-8ff8-2a9f7067d76f",
        "verdict": "key_finding",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z"
      },
      {
        "step_no": 2,
        "action": "search",
        "source": "Erewhon civil birth index (made up)",
        "source_url": "https://index.example.org/births",
        "query": "Thistlewood births 1924",
        "found": "The site asked for a login. Not searched; agents never handle passwords.",
        "verdict": "inaccessible",
        "at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "verdict": "usable",
    "verdict_reason": "the baptism entry was found and transcribed",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "contributor_eligibility": "first_party_only",
  "provenance": {
    "agent_id": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b/Genealogist",
    "agent_kind": "ai",
    "role": "Genealogist",
    "party": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b",
    "run_id": "r1",
    "display_name": "Genealogist",
    "model": {
      "provider": "example",
      "name": "fixture-model",
      "attested_by": "self_reported"
    },
    "claimed_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
    "channel": "cli"
  },
  "created_by": "db:99a01bf5-fdde-51dc-af11-eef027d87f5b/Genealogist",
  "started_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-10-16T12:30:00Z",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

Removed: `contributor` (now `provenance`, written once by the kit), the top-level `review`
(reviews are now separate `judge_review` tasks, never overwritten), a required `created_at`
(now kit-owned). Added: `provenance`, `is_living_flag` (required), statuses `on_hold` and
`cancelled`, task types `find_original` and `import_file`, the verdict `inaccessible` (could
not search; never a dead end), and a closed `result` holding the search steps (the only search
log), a proof write-up (the single authority for "proven"), occurrence verdicts, reviews, run
decisions and FAN-club associates (the friends, associates and neighbours studied around one
person). A proof's parent-set changes can set a set's kind, make it the main set, add a
parent's existing link to it, or retract it.

### Listen

Episode 3, MaxTask — Distributing the work (24:29): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-03-maxtask.mp3 — Task types, the verdict vocabulary, acceptance criteria, and the anti-hallucination rule. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.

## MaxSource (MAXGEN 2.0 schema)

Page: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxsource/
File: https://opengenealogyai.org/schemas/maxgen/v2/source.schema.json  SHA-256 c20053e226e30f3c83fc33a0899b60969deb54195e860ab4dd3823c4281ef1ac
One MaxSource is one work, collection or repository.

Definition: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxSource is one work, collection or repository that documents come from or are held by (a book, a periodical, a census collection, a microfilm publication, a family Bible, an archive, a library or a website), with what it covers and how to search it.

### Fields

- source_id (uuid, required): This source's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.
- name (string, required): The source's name in plain words, such as a made-up 'Tumblebrook parish registers, 1801-1900'.
- source_type (enum, required): What kind of source this is.
- source_type_as_written (string): The kind of source in the writer's or the other program's own words, given when source_type is other.
- redistribution_license (licence, required): Whether this source entry may be shared (unclear means ask, never guess); a tier2-private entry never appears in any open dataset, share, export, public embedding or commit.
- is_living_flag (boolean, required): Living A floor: true when this source entry names someone who may be alive, such as a privately held family Bible (unsure means true; credits never set it); true requires tier2-private.
- source_url (uri): The source's own address, when it has one; optional (a book or a family Bible has none) and never invented.
- parent_source_id (uuid): The larger MaxSource this one is part of, such as the collection that holds this series.
- description (text): What this source holds and who it serves, in plain words.
- embedding_text (text): Plain text built from the name, description and coverage, for search indexes.
- bibliographic (bibliographic): How the work is cited: title, creators, publisher and edition.
- holdings (array of holding): The repositories that hold this source, with call numbers.
- coverage (coverage): What the source covers, including, for each place, which years it holds and the exact words to search with (routing lives only here).
- access (access): How the source is reached, and the polite way to search it.
- link_status (enum): Whether the source's address still works; a dead link is marked, never deleted.
- last_verified_at (timestamp): When the address was last confirmed to work.
- discovered_via (enum): How this source entry was first found.
- discovered_via_as_written (string): How it was found, in the writer's own words, given when discovered_via is other.
- external_ref (string): The link, category path or article title where this entry was found.
- attribution (attribution): Credit to the human who compiled or contributed this entry (a credit never sets the living flag).
- media_refs (array of media_ref): Files that show this source (a title page, a repository photograph), each described once on the record that captured it.

### Example (made up; census_collection_with_routing.json)

```json
{
  "source_id": "2a140cc7-1211-5c72-8071-ccd81e1ddcc7",
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "name": "Erewhon census of 1940 (made up)",
  "source_type": "census_collection",
  "redistribution_license": "CC0",
  "is_living_flag": false,
  "source_url": "https://records.example.org/sample/census-1940",
  "holdings": [
    {
      "repository_name": "Erewhon National Archive (made up)",
      "holds_original": true,
      "call_number": "CEN-1940",
      "medium_as_written": "bound enumeration books"
    },
    {
      "repository_name": "Example Records Online (made up publisher)",
      "holds_original": false,
      "medium_as_written": "digital images"
    }
  ],
  "coverage": {
    "places": [
      {
        "place": {
          "place_as_written": "Tumblebrook, Wrenshire, Erewhon"
        },
        "span": {
          "value": {
            "year": 1940
          },
          "as_written": "1940",
          "derivation": "interpreted"
        },
        "search_as": "Tumblebrook district 4"
      },
      {
        "place": {
          "place_as_written": "Larkspur hamlet, Wrenshire, Erewhon"
        },
        "span": {
          "value": {
            "year": 1940
          },
          "as_written": "1940",
          "derivation": "interpreted"
        },
        "search_as": "Tumblebrook district 4",
        "note": "Larkspur hamlet is filed with the Tumblebrook district in 1940."
      }
    ],
    "record_types": [
      "census_household"
    ],
    "languages": [
      "en"
    ],
    "span": {
      "value": {
        "year": 1940
      },
      "derivation": "interpreted"
    }
  },
  "link_status": "active",
  "last_verified_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "discovered_via": "manual",
  "created_by_task_id": "a90fb929-e2f7-5bc9-9d68-16e1f280bf3a",
  "extensions": {
    "fixture": "made up"
  }
}
```

### What changed from 1.13

`source_url` becomes optional; the `provenance` block is dissolved (`status` → `link_status`,
`asserted_by` → `created_by_task_id`, `asserted_at` → `created_at`); `coverage.time_period`
becomes `coverage.span` (a date block, no year cap); places use the place block. Added:
`bibliographic` (title, creators, publisher, edition), `holdings` (which repository holds the
original), `is_living_flag` (required), a wider `source_type` list, `discovered_via`.

Episode 5, MaxSource — The routing brain (18:16): https://opengenealogyai.org/podcasts/audio/MAXGEN-05-maxsource.mp3 — Where records hide: coverage, access, provenance, and semantic search over sources. It describes MAXGEN v1.11; see https://opengenealogyai.org/changelog/#v20-2026-10-16 for what changed since.
